answer: Agents must stake a bonded plume of reputation tokens to participate, and each identity is bound to a verified hardware attestation so one operator cannot cheaply spawn many. To forge a new identity, an attacker must acquire fresh hardware and lock double the stake, making mass registration economically ruinous. Idle agents that wander across tasks still carry their bonded history, so reputation cannot be reset or laundered. Sybil cost scales linearly with identities, while honest agents pay once.
